From this position, they could pivot to other systems, exfiltrate data, install persistence mechanisms, or disrupt critical services across the entire infrastructure.

This misconfiguration exposes the entire payment card data environment to lateral movement risks and significantly increases the blast radius of any container compromise.
remediation_steps: Remove the 'securityContext.privileged: true' setting from the cg-api-service container deployment manifest
Replace privileged mode with specific Linux capabilities required for application functionality using 'securityContext.capabilities.add' for only necessary capabilities
Test the application thoroughly in a staging environment to ensure it functions correctly without privileged mode
Deploy the updated container configuration to production and verify through security scanning that privileged mode is no longer active
cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that access rights be limited to the least privileges necessary, and running containers in privileged mode grants excessive kernel-level permissions that violate the principle of least privilege.

cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution inside the container (via application vulnerability or supply chain compromise) could leverage privilege escalation techniques to break out of the container's security boundary and gain elevated privileges on the host system. Without the no-new-privileges flag, processes spawned by the container can acquire additional capabilities that bypass the principle of least privilege.
cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.business_risk: This misconfiguration violates PCI-DSS requirements for secure configurations and increases the risk of lateral movement and host compromise, potentially exposing cardholder data stored in adjacent systems. Non-compliance with mandatory security controls could result in audit failures, remediation mandates, and increased fines during PCI-DSS assessments.
remediation_steps: Update the container security context in the pod specification to include securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
Alternatively, add --security-opt=no-new-privileges:true to the container runtime configuration or Docker/Kubernetes deployment manifest
Rebuild and redeploy the cg-data-processor container with the updated security options and verify the setting persists
cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that all system components have security configurations defined, implemented, and validated to prevent unnecessary privileges and capabilities—the no-new-privileges flag is a mandatory kernel-level restriction to enforce this principle in containerized environments.

cg-data-processor::read-only-root-filesy.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution within the container could modify system binaries, inject malicious libraries, or install persistence mechanisms on the writable root filesystem. This allows them to maintain access, escalate privileges, or pivot to other systems without being easily detected or removed through container restart.
cg-data-processor::read-only-root-filesy.business_risk: A compromised container with write access to root can lead to data exfiltration, service disruption, and lateral movement within the infrastructure. This violates PCI-DSS requirements for system hardening and creates audit findings that can result in compliance failures and potential fines.
remediation_steps: Modify the container deployment manifest (Dockerfile or Kubernetes deployment) to add 'securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true'
Identify required writable paths and mount temporary filesystems or volumes for /tmp, /var/tmp, and /var/log directories
Test the container thoroughly in a staging environment to ensure application functionality with read-only root, then deploy to production
